entities.summary:
The February 2011 Christchurch earthquake was a devastating seismic event that struck New Zealand on February 22, 2011. The magnitude 6.3 earthquake caused widespread destruction in Christchurch, killing 185 people and injuring thousands more. The earthquake also caused significant economic losses, with estimated damages reaching over $40 billion.

The earthquake had a profound impact on the city of Christchurch, leading to a major reconstruction effort and changes to building codes and emergency preparedness measures. The event also highlighted the need for improved disaster resilience and mitigation strategies in New Zealand.

The legacy of the earthquake can be seen in the many memorial sites and memorials that have been erected in Christchurch, including the Christchurch Earthquake National Memorial. The event also led to changes in the way that emergency services respond to natural disasters, with improved coordination and communication between agencies.

The earthquake was a turning point for New Zealand, marking a new era of disaster resilience and preparedness.
